meta.notes: Country-agnostic sample for the agriculture / methane-reduction buyer group (rice methane, regenerative soil carbon, livestock/manure) — biochar deliberately excluded. Buyers, roles, volumes and SBTi/industry were verified against public announcements. Anchored on two landmark, well-documented deals: Amazon's 685,000 tCO2e offtake of rice-methane (AWD) credits from The Good Rice Alliance (a Bayer/GenZero/Shell venture) in India, and Microsoft's 2.85M-tonne regenerative soil-carbon deal with Indigo in the US. Findings are mapped to the real registered projects in our dataset (Bayer's Gold Standard India rice projects GS12305/GS12306; Indigo Carbon's CAR1459).

Pursues climate goals via its own Climate Pledge (net-zero 2040) rather than SBTi-validated targets.

buyer_profiles.sbti_status: Near-term targets set; carbon-negative by 2030 commitment
buyer_profiles.profile_summary: Software & cloud company and the largest voluntary buyer of carbon removal. Signed a 12-year, 2.85 million-tonne regenerative soil-carbon agreement with Indigo (its third Indigo deal, after 40k t in 2024 and 60k t in 2025) to help meet its carbon-negative-by-2030 goal.

Life-sciences and crop-science group; registered developer of the Gold Standard India rice-methane (AWD) projects and a co-owner of The Good Rice Alliance (with GenZero and Shell). Acts here as programme developer/partner rather than an end buyer.
Temasek-backed decarbonisation investment platform; co-owner/investor in The Good Rice Alliance, financing the scale-up of India rice-methane reduction. Investor/funder, not a credit end buyer.
Global energy group; co-owner/investor in The Good Rice Alliance and an active carbon-credit trader. Investor/funder in the rice-methane venture here. Does not hold SBTi-validated targets.

US agtech company running 'Carbon by Indigo', a large regenerative-agriculture soil-carbon programme (cover crops, reduced tillage, nitrogen timing). Registered developer of CAR1459 and Microsoft's counterparty; developer/seller, not the retiring end buyer.

buyer_findings.volume_basis: 685,000+ tCO2e committed across The Good Rice Alliance's initial crediting phase (India rice-methane, AWD water management). Attributed at programme level to Bayer's Gold Standard India rice-methane projects.
buyer_findings.evidence_summary: Amazon signed a long-term offtake with The Good Rice Alliance (owned by Bayer, GenZero and Shell) for 685,000+ tCO2e of methane-reduction credits from smallholder rice farming in India via alternate wetting-and-drying. Bayer Bioscience is the registered developer of this Gold Standard India rice-methane project; attribution is programme-level.
GenZero (Temasek-backed) is a co-owner of The Good Rice Alliance, financing the India rice-methane programme behind these credits. Investor/funder at programme level.
Shell is a co-owner of The Good Rice Alliance (with Bayer and GenZero). Investor/funder in the rice-methane venture; programme-level attribution.

Bayer Bioscience Private Limited is the registered developer of this Gold Standard India rice-methane project and a co-owner of The Good Rice Alliance (with GenZero and Shell), running AWD water-management across 13,000+ smallholder farmers.

buyer_findings.volume_basis: 2.85 million tCO2e over a 12-year agreement under the Carbon by Indigo regenerative-agriculture programme (following 40,000 t in 2024 and 60,000 t in 2025).
buyer_findings.evidence_summary: Indigo agreed to sell Microsoft 2.85 million tonnes of soil-carbon removals over 12 years from the US-based Carbon by Indigo programme (cover crops, reduced tillage, improved nitrogen timing) — the largest soil-carbon transaction to date and Microsoft's third Indigo deal.
Indigo Carbon PBC is the registered developer of CAR1459 and Microsoft's counterparty under the Carbon by Indigo programme. Developer/seller rather than a retiring end buyer.

risks.risk_description: AWD (alternate wetting-and-drying) rice-methane crediting relies on modelled emission factors and field-water monitoring across thousands of smallholder plots; quantification and additionality of avoided methane are an active area of methodology scrutiny.
risks.ai_summary: Smallholder AWD rice-methane quantification (MRV) and additionality remain a recognised scrutiny area for these credits.

risks.risk_description: Project is 'Listed' (pre/early issuance). Delivering against a 685,000 tCO2e multi-year offtake depends on scaling AWD adoption across 13,000+ farmers and 35,000+ ha, so forward volumes carry delivery/timing risk.
risks.ai_summary: Large forward offtake against an early-stage smallholder programme — delivery/timing risk on the committed volume.

risks.risk_description: Soil-carbon sequestration is impermanent and reversible (tillage, land-use change, drought can release stored carbon); durability and the risk of reversal are the central integrity questions for regenerative-agriculture credits.
risks.ai_summary: Soil carbon is reversible; permanence/reversal is the key integrity risk for regenerative-agriculture removals.

risks.risk_description: Soil-carbon quantification blends sparse soil sampling with modelling; measurement uncertainty and over-crediting exposure are recognised concerns even under the Climate Action Reserve Soil Enrichment Protocol.
risks.ai_summary: Sampling-plus-model soil-carbon MRV carries measurement uncertainty / over-crediting exposure.
